name: refusing to cover others' work
gloss: Members keep the room's work off others' art: going around it, sparing it, sizing the work so it does not cover a neighbour.
must_show: Restraint toward others' work kept by the room's own choice: going around a neighbour's design, refusing to overwrite it, sizing or placing the work to spare it, respect for others' effort stated.
must_not_show: Moving because a neighbour asked (T3-039); reining in the room's members who are already attacking (T3-076); restraint written into a script (T3-168); an agreed border (T3-010).
decide_when_both: Restraint inside a border deal: T3-010 primary when the deal leads, T3-024 added when the restraint has concepts of its own. Sparing others' work by the room's own choice is T3-024; agreeing lines with a neighbour is T3-010.

discriminators.question: Is a line or space agreed with a neighbour (T3-010), or others' work spared by the room's own choice (T3-024)?
Does the room yield when asked (T3-039), or keep off others' work unasked (T3-024)?
Is an attack under way stopped (T3-076), or others' work spared before any attack (T3-024)?
Is the fairness of covering argued (T3-046), or covering simply refused (T3-024)?
Is the restraint kept by hand (T3-024), or written into a script (T3-168)?

varies: From going around someone's chequered tiles to a room's rule of peace toward its neighbours' mascots.
is_not: A room moving its work after a neighbour asks for the space (T3-039).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-010 in practice (69 bag lines keep T3-010); it stays its own because restraint without any agreement is common and readers can see whether a deal was made.

exemplars.quote: Going around someone's chequered tiles so not to spoil their design
Snek is happy to live in peace with anyone we can. We can curve around the corner of the AMD logo
Don't wanna destroy other people's work.

name: yielding space when asked
old_label: yielding space when a neighbour asks
gloss: The room gives ground when a neighbour asks: moving, shifting or shrinking its work, giving a spot back.
must_show: A neighbour's request for space and the room yielding: moving the work over, shifting it, shrinking it, letting the neighbour take the spot back, forfeiting an attempt.
must_not_show: Refusing to yield (T3-123); moving after the work was lost to an attack (T3-022); restraint with no request (T3-024).
decide_when_both: Yielding inside a border deal: T3-010 primary when the deal leads (57 bag lines keep T3-010), T3-039 added when the yielding has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Does the room yield the space (T3-039), or refuse (T3-123)?
Does the room move because a neighbour asked (T3-039), or because its work was lost (T3-022)?
Does the room yield to a request (T3-039), or spare others' work unasked (T3-024)?
Does the room give up its own space (T3-039), or grant a neighbour room on its work (T3-012)?
Is a line or space settled between neighbours (T3-010), or the room's work moved, shrunk or given up because a neighbour asked (T3-039)?

varies: From a sign moved a few pixels left to a whole attempt forfeited to another room.
is_not: Moving the work after an attack destroyed it (T3-022).
two_or_half: See T3-123: the yielding half of one kind, kept two by which way the room went.

exemplars.quote: we should just move the libra/terezi sign to the left and let university of toronto take it back
we've successfully moved them from one-over-the-other to a side-by-side
I forfeit my attempt at Totoro

name: apologizing to neighbours for damage
old_label: apologizing to a neighbour for damage
gloss: Members apologise to a neighbouring room for damage the room or its members did to its work, often offering to help repair it.
must_show: An apology to another room for damage to its work by the room or people from it: 'sorry about that', apologies made in the other room's thread, offers to help redraw or rebuild.
must_not_show: Owning a mistake inside the room's own or an ally's work (T3-170); mourning art the room covered with no apology to its owners (T3-183).
decide_when_both: Apology inside a deal: T3-010 primary when the deal leads (68 bag lines), T3-040 added when the apology has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Is damage to a neighbour's work apologised for (T3-040), or a friendly mistake inside the room's own or allied work owned (T3-170)?
Is the apology made to the neighbour (T3-040), or the covered art mourned among members (T3-183)?
Is the damage apologised for (T3-040), or the attackers stopped (T3-076)?
Is damage to a neighbour's work apologised for (T3-040), or a quarrel between the subs closed (T3-047)?
Do the former attackers only apologise (T3-040), or help repair (T3-119)?
Is a line or space settled between neighbours (T3-010), or damage the room did to a neighbour's work apologised for (T3-040)?

varies: From a one-line 'I'm so sorry' to offers to redraw the character nearby; apologies made on behalf of a nation's members.
is_not: A member admitting a misclick in the room's own work (T3-170).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-010 in practice (68 bag lines); kept apart because an apology without any deal is common.

exemplars.quote: Sorry about that, if you have the reference pixel art, some of us might be able to help you draw it nearby
We're as sorry as Canadians that we forced you to relocate.
I wanted to apologize, for what it's worth, for all of the asshole people from our subreddit that attacked you.

name: arguing whether covering is fair
old_label: arguing whether covering others' work is fair
gloss: Members argue whether covering others' work is fair: an open canvas where anything goes, or a wrong done to others' effort.
must_show: Argument over covering others' work as such: 'it's an open canvas', 'that's the whole point', 'they put in passion, respect it', whether a neighbour may use the room's background.
must_not_show: Refusing to cover with no argument (T3-024); pleading to have one's own work spared (T3-139); arguing who had the spot first (T3-045).
decide_when_both: An argument that ends in restraint: T3-046 when the argument leads, T3-024 when the restraint does. Stopping the room's own attack is T3-076; arguing whether such covering is fair is T3-046.

discriminators.question: Is covering refused (T3-024), or its fairness argued (T3-046)?
Is the room's attack stopped (T3-076), or the fairness of covering argued (T3-046)?
Does the speaker plead for their own work (T3-139), or argue whether covering is fair (T3-046)?
Is who came first argued (T3-045), or whether covering is fair at all (T3-046)?

varies: From a Void member calling erasure the point of the experiment to members weighing whether a neighbour may use their blank background.
is_not: A member pleading that a rival spare their room's logo (T3-139).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-024 and of T3-006 in subject; kept apart because the argument itself, with sides, is the doing.

exemplars.quote: Lol why did you think it was ruining it - the black void was central to the experiment.
C'è gente che c'ha messo dedizione, passione e creatività. Io questo lo rispetto
it seems silly to not let them go into our blank blue background.

name: reining in the room's attackers
old_label: reining in the room's own attackers
gloss: Members tell their own room's attackers to stop: no more attacks, leave the neighbours alone, stop vandalising.
must_show: The room's own members told to stop attacking or vandalising others' work, or an attack called off after an objection; rules against new wars.
must_not_show: Restraint before any attack (T3-024); pleading with another room's attackers (T3-139); excluding members as a sanction (T3-121); members acting against such a call (T3-102).
decide_when_both: An attack called for and then reined in: T3-006 primary when the attacking leads, T3-076 when the reining in does (rule 0 pairs them both ways).

discriminators.question: Is an attack under way stopped (T3-076), or others' work spared before any attack (T3-024)?
Are the room's own attackers stopped (T3-076), or another room's attackers asked to stop (T3-139)?
Is the room's call to hold back made (T3-076), or defied (T3-102)?
Does the room rein in its own attackers (T3-076), or say the attackers are not its own (T3-188)?
Is the attack stopped (T3-076), or the fairness of covering argued (T3-046)?
Does the room stop its own attackers (T3-076), or hold another room to an agreement (T3-195)?
Is an attack called for (T3-006), or reined in (T3-076)?
Is an attack the room started stopped (T3-076), or retaliation for damage it suffered declined (T3-007)?
Is the damage apologised for (T3-040), or the attackers stopped (T3-076)?
Is the room's own attack on others stopped (T3-076), or upkeep put before expansion (T3-042)?
Is the room's attack reined in by words (T3-076), or a member excluded (T3-121)?

varies: From one 'stop messing with other schools' to moderators' rules against new wars; attacks withdrawn after an objection.
is_not: A member asking another room's raiders to stop (T3-139).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-024, restraint; kept apart because an attack under way is stopped, which restraint before any attack does not show.

exemplars.quote: No, stop messing with other schools
Alot of people from this sub are vandalizing the art on place, this is getting annoying
SEGERA HENTIKAN SERANGAN KE INTRODWARF

name: defying the call for restraint
old_label: defying the room's call to hold back
gloss: A member goes on attacking or breaks a treaty after the room told them to hold back.
must_show: A member refusing the room's restraint: attacking after being told no, calling to break the room's treaty, refusing to stop drawing over a neighbour.
must_not_show: The room's call to hold back itself (T3-076); attacks the room calls for (T3-006).
decide_when_both: A call to hold back and its defiance in one theme: the side with more concepts is primary, the other under rule 0.

discriminators.question: Is the call to hold back made (T3-076), or defied (T3-102)?
Is the attack called for by the room (T3-006), or pressed by a member against the room's word (T3-102)?
Is a room held to its agreement (T3-195), or does a member break it (T3-102)?

varies: From 'Nah I'm going to hit the Bills' to a call to break a treaty.
is_not: A room calling for an attack on a rival (T3-006).
two_or_half: It is the other half of T3-076; kept apart because the member acts against the room's call.

exemplars.quote: Nah I'm going to hit the bills with green
we have to break the treaty now
Never shall i stop drawing balrog.

name: mourning art the room covered
gloss: Members mourn or regret art that their own room's work covered.
must_show: Grief or regret among members for another's art the room's own work displaced: 'RIP Blonde', a memorial post for a neighbour the room's expansion left no room for, members torn between the two works.
must_not_show: Apologising to the neighbour (T3-040); mourning the room's own lost work (T3-029).
decide_when_both: Mourning and apology together: T3-040 when the apology is addressed to the neighbour, T3-183 when the mourning stays among members.

discriminators.question: Is the room's own lost work mourned (T3-029), or others' art the room covered (T3-183)?
Is the regret addressed to the neighbour as an apology (T3-040), or voiced among members (T3-183)?

varies: From a one-line 'RIP' to a member who worked on both the flag and the tree it covered.
is_not: Members mourning their own room's erased logo (T3-029).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-029 in mood and half of T3-040 in object; kept apart because the room grieves harm it did itself.
